text: dsh-qq-skin 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 QQ 风格界面插件。它通过主题 token 覆盖和运行时注入的布局样式，把聊天流、消息气泡、助手卡片、输入区、时间戳与滚动条调整为 QQ NT 风格，并保留宿主明暗主题偏好。用户可在设置行切换五种色板、气泡尾巴、助手头像、聊天宽度、提示音和打字动效；设置会持久化并热更新。适合希望自定义 DSH 网页聊天外观的用户，使用 dsh 0.2 及以上版本安装到 web profile。

dsh-qq-skin adds a QQ-style look to the DSH Web client using theme tokens and injected chat layout styles. Choose five palettes and adjust bubbles, avatars, chat width, sounds, and typing effects in persistent settings. Changes hot-reload. Requires DSH 0.2 or later.

dsh-qq-skin 的功能「色板切换」：用户可从设置行选择 classic、vivid、clean、green 或 black 色板，插件据此重建主题 token 覆盖并即时呈现。
dsh-qq-skin 的功能「聊天布局」：插件注入布局样式，调整聊天流宽度、用户气泡尾巴、助手头像卡片、输入区、时间戳与滚动条；尾巴、头像和宽度可调。
dsh-qq-skin 的功能「可视化设置与热更新」：General 设置区提供 QQ 皮肤设置行，写入色板及显示选项；配置变化会重挂主题与布局层，无需重启插件。
dsh-qq-skin 的功能「新消息提示音」：开启 messageSound 后，客户端观察聊天流中新出现的助手消息节点，并用 Web Audio 合成短提示音；默认关闭。

dsh-qq-skin README · dsh-qq-skin：A **QQ NT messenger skin** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). Light and dark share one QQ NT language — **light mode is clean and restrained** (near-white surfaces, neutral borders/hover, brand blue `#12B7F5` and light-blue bubbles `#A8E3FF` as recognition accents), **dark mode is a calm blue-gray** (base `#101822`, desaturated, blue reserved for accents), instantly recognizable. Ships with five palette variants (Classic Blue / Vivid Purple / Clean White / Green Bubble / Deep Black), configurable toggles and sizing, plus a settings-panel visual switcher with hot reload.

dsh-qq-skin README · dsh-qq-skin：> **How it works.** The skin is two reversible layers; it never registers a new theme id and never touches the user's Light/Dark/System preference.
> - **Token layer** — stacks one `--dsw-*` semantic-token override via `ctx.theme.overrideTokens('dsh-qq-skin', ...)`. Every token carries a `{ light, dark }` pair, so the skin follows the active base palette instead of fighting it. Light mode runs blue through surfaces, borders, interactions, and scrollbars; the dark palette is a `#101822`-based calm blue-gray scale where blue only accents (brand, bubbles, primary buttons). The set is generated per palette (`buildTokenOverrides(palette)`): the five palettes share the neutral blue-gray skeleton and differ only in the personality tokens.
> - **Layout layer** — injects one global `<style>` tag (`qq-layout.ts`) for geometry and structure: the chat flow is centered and narrowed, user bubbles are light blue with a "tail", assistant rows get an avatar disc + white card (matched via `data-chat-flow-kind='assistant-step'`), the input area becomes a capsule, plus a slim conversation-header divider, QQ-styled timestamps and scrollbar, and sidebar session-row hover

dsh-qq-skin README · Configuration：The plugin receives config the cordis function-plugin way (`apply(ctx, config)`); unset fields fall back to defaults:

| --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | `'classic'` | Palette variant: `classic` Classic Blue / `vivid` Vivid Purple / `clean` Clean White / `green` Green Bubble / `black` Deep Black |
| `bubbleTail` | `true` | Small triangular "tail" on the right of user bubbles |
| `assistantAvatar` | `true` | Official QQ-penguin avatar disc left of assistant messages |

dsh-qq-skin README · What it covers：Tokens that are **not** overridden keep the product default, so a QQ-skin run stays readable and consistent everywhere else.
dsh-qq-skin README · Requirements (dsh version)：Built and run against **deepseek-harness (`dsh`) 0.2.0 or later**. dsh 0.2 changed two settings-system contracts (2026-10):

dsh-qq-skin README · Requirements (dsh version)：- **The settings namespace IS the profile entry id.** `ctx.settings.register(ns, schema)` is gone: the plugin's settings schema is now the `Config` export of its host entry, and **every field must be `.volatile()`** — the settings panel projects volatile fields only, so a non-volatile field appears in no descriptor and accepts no write. The namespace comes from the `id` of the entry in `cordis.patch.yml` (`qq-skin`), not from a string the plugin picks.
- **The browser half reads and writes settings through `ctx.configForms`.** The `ctx.settingsScope` service is gone: the client uses `ctx.configForms.get('qq-skin')`, whose snapshot value is the fully resolved host config (schema defaults → profile config → user edits) and whose `set(field, value)` persists an edit. A 0.2 client entry no longer receives a `config` argument at all, so the built-in defaults only cover the first frame.
- The skin ships its own settings row in the General section, hence the host half calls `settings.configure({ auto: false })` to suppress the auto-generated page.
dsh-qq-skin README · Requirements (dsh version)：Earlier dsh versions (0.1.x) are not compatible: they have no `settings.configure`, no `ctx.configForms`, and no volatile config projection.

dsh-qq-skin README · Install：One command installs the plugin into the `web` profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-qq-skin
```

dsh-qq-skin README · Install：That is the whole flow: `dsh plugin` initializes the profile on first use,
runs `pnpm add dsh-qq-skin` inside the profile directory, then reconciles the
profile's bundle layer against the installed state — because `dsh-qq-skin`
declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (→ `cordis.patch.yml`), it joins the bundle stack
automatically. The next `dsh web` boot composes it, the client bundle loads,
and the skin stacks as soon as `ui-theme` is active.

dsh-qq-skin README · Install：Installing from a local checkout (path specs are anchored to your invoking
directory; `link:` keeps the live checkout linked):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ../dsh-qq-skin
dsh plugin --profile web add link:../dsh-qq-skin
```

Removing is equally one command:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-qq-skin
```

dsh-qq-skin README · Install：The plugin declares `dsh.client` with `platform: web` and injects the `theme`,
`slots`, `locale`, `remote`, and `configForms` services, so the Web boot loads
its client bundle and applies the layer as soon as `ui-theme` is active.

dsh-qq-skin README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test            # vitest (token shape + layout injection + runtime hot reload + settings wiring)
pnpm run build       # tsc + tsdown → lib/index.js (host) + lib/client.js (browser closure-factory)

dsh-qq-skin README · Development：The client bundle is produced by the same two-face layout as the harness
`clientBundle` preset: `lib/index.js` is the plain ESM host row, `lib/client.js`
is the `window.__ModuleLoader__` closure-factory the Web boot consumes. No
build-time CSS pipeline is needed: the layout styles ship as an inline string
inside the client bundle (`QQ_LAYOUT_CSS` in `qq-layout.ts`) and are injected at
runtime via `document.createElement('style')` — the same shape as ui-theme's
`installThemeStyles` — then removed on effect dispose. Layout selectors rely on
the client CSS Modules `[hash]_[local]` naming (`[class$="_localName"]`
suffix matches) and the components' own `data-*` hooks, never on build-time
hash values.

dsh-qq-skin README · Development：The settings row (`settings-row.tsx`) uses inline token styles reading `--dsw-*`
directly, so it adds no CSS Modules pipeline; `react` and the collaboration
services stay external to the client bundle and resolve through the platform
module table.
